legal.headline: Rehabilitation delayed may amount to rehabilitation denied: Supreme Court issues directions on bonded labour
legal.hook: Supreme Court issued pan-India directions for the effective identification, rescue and rehabilitation of bonded labourers, mandating disbursement of immediate financial assistance within 7 days of issuance of release…
legal.summary: Supreme Court issued pan-India directions for the effective identification, rescue and rehabilitation of bonded labourers, mandating disbursement of immediate financial assistance within 7 days of issuance of release… Observing that identification, release and rehabilitation are interconnected stages of a continuing constitutional responsibility under Articles 21 and 23 of the Constitution , the Court held that rehabilitation delayed may, in substance, amount to rehabilitation denied. The Court further observed that the principal concern was not the absence of a statutory framework under the Bonded Labour System (Abolition) Act, 1976 , but the difficulties encountered in its effective implementation, particularly in cases involving inter-State rescue and repatriation.
legal.contextNote: The Supreme Court, invoking Articles 21 and 23 of the Constitution, issued pan‑India directions for the identification, rescue and rehabilitation of bonded labourers, mandating that financial assistance be disbursed within 7 days of a release order.
